# No Content-Security-Policy on the hosted auth pages

- **Kind**: chore (security hardening)
- **Date**: 2026-07-30
- **Requested by**: Ian
- **Source**: red-team pass while scoping #943 (handoff allowlist), 2026-07-30

Apply rules: django-mojo-build-conventions

## Description

`grep -rni "content-security-policy" mojo/` returns **nothing** — the framework sets
no CSP header on any response, including the hosted auth pages
(`mojo/apps/account/templates/account/auth_base.html`), which are the highest-value
pages it serves: they hold access and refresh tokens in `localStorage`.

This is defense-in-depth, not a live vulnerability on its own. It surfaced because
the absence of a CSP is what made the `?back=` sink in #943 (unvalidated
`backEl.href = paramBack`, `auth_base.html:196-198`) directly exploitable rather than
merely untidy. #943 fixes that specific sink; a CSP would have blunted it and would
blunt the next one.

## Context

A `script-src` policy without `unsafe-inline` is **not** a drop-in here: `auth_base.html`
carries a large inline `<script>` block plus `{{ login_methods|json_script:... }}`.
Adopting a strict policy means either nonce-ing those blocks or moving them into
`mojo-auth.js` — real work, which is why this is its own item rather than a line in #943.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A CSP is set on the hosted auth pages, at minimum constraining `script-src`,
      `frame-ancestors`, and `form-action`
- [ ] Inline scripts in `auth_base.html` are nonce'd or relocated — no blanket
      `unsafe-inline`
- [ ] Deployments can extend/override the policy by setting (whitelabel deployments
      load their own assets)
- [ ] Tests assert the header is present and that a known-bad inline injection is
      blocked by the policy
- [ ] Docs: django_developer security section + settings reference; CHANGELOG

## Investigation

- **What exists**: nothing — no CSP anywhere in `mojo/`. Stronger: no `X-Frame-Options`,
  `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` or `Permissions-Policy` either. The
  framework sets **no** security headers at all.
- **Related**: #943 (handoff destination allowlist + `?back=` scheme check)
- **Out of scope**: CSP for consuming applications' own pages — deployments own those

---

## Plan

**Objective.** Emit a `Content-Security-Policy` header on exactly the four
framework-hosted auth pages (the templates extending `account/auth_base.html`), with a
per-request nonce on every inline `<script>` and no `unsafe-inline` in `script-src`.
Whitelabel asset loading (logos, hero images, tenant CSS, cross-origin `api_base`) keeps
working untouched, and a deployment can extend, weaken, report-only, or disable the
policy from settings.

### D1 — Nonce the inline scripts; do NOT relocate them into `mojo-auth.js`

- The `auth_base.html` inline block (~215 lines) is saturated with Django interpolation
  (`{{ api_base }}`, `{{ success_redirect }}`, `{{ passkey_prompt|escapejs }}`,
  `{{ group_uuid|escapejs }}`, `{{ skip_session_check|yesno }}`). Relocating means
  inventing a config-blob contract and rewriting the `mojo-auth.js` bootstrap.
- Relocation is pointless unless the **child** blocks move too (`login.html`,
  `register.html`, `passkey_enroll.html`, `contact.html` are all inline as well) —
  otherwise `unsafe-inline` is still required.
- Decisive for this batch: nonce-ing changes only the `<script>` **open tag**. It never
  touches a line inside the IIFE, so #943's fixed `.catch()` and `?back=` scheme check
  ride along untouched. Relocation would require re-typing that code — the exact way to
  resurrect the pre-#943 version.

### D2 — Policy (fixed directive order → byte-stable, assertable header)

```
default-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors <per-page>;
form-action 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<32 hex>';
style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https:[ <api_origin>]; img-src * data:;
font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'[ <api_origin>]
```

- `script-src`: nonce + `'self'`, no `unsafe-inline`, no scheme wildcard. The **external**
  `<script src="{{ api_base }}/api/account/static/mojo-auth.js">` also gets the nonce — a
  nonce match allows an external load regardless of origin, so a cross-origin `api_base`
  needs no host source here.
- `form-action 'self'`: every form in `login.html` / `register.html` / `contact.html` is
  JS-handled with no `action=` attribute (verified).
- `base-uri 'none'` / `object-src 'none'`: no `<base>`, no `<object>` in any auth template.
- `style-src ... 'unsafe-inline'`: **required** — 10 style-attribute sites across 6
  templates plus `<style>{{ custom_css|safe }}</style>`. Do **not** put a nonce in
  `style-src`: a nonce there makes browsers ignore `'unsafe-inline'` and would break every
  style attribute. `https:` covers `custom_css_url` (already https-validated by
  `auth_config._validate_https_url`); the `api_origin` term covers an http dev `api_base`
  serving `mojo-auth-theme.css`.
- `img-src * data:`: `logo_url` / `hero_image_url` / `favicon_url` are tenant-supplied with
  **no** scheme validation, so any origin restriction guarantees tenant breakage for
  near-zero gain once `script-src` is nonce-locked. `data:` because `validate_custom_css`
  explicitly permits data URIs.
- `connect-src 'self' <api_origin>`: `mojo-auth.js` fetches only `_baseURL`, and
  `contact.html` issues its own `fetch(submitUrl, ...)` built from the same `api_base`
  (see Challenge O4). No `eval`, no dynamic script injection anywhere.
- `font-src 'self' data:`: no CDN fonts, no `@import`, no `@font-face` in the theme CSS.
- No `report-uri` by default (no endpoint ships); a deployment adds one via the override
  setting.

### D3 — `frame-ancestors` is per-page, NOT a single global value

`'none'` on **login / register / passkey** — the pages that hold tokens in `localStorage`.
**Omitted entirely on `/contact`**, because `docs/web_developer/account/public_messages.md:221`
documents embedding `/contact?kind=<kind>` in an iframe as the *recommended* integration
for an external marketing site. See Challenge O1 — this is the difference between a
security win and breaking a documented consumer integration. Implement as a
`frame_ancestors` argument to `default_directives()` / `build_policy()`, defaulting to
`'none'`, passed as `""` (drop the directive) by the contact render site only.

### D4 — `{{ login_methods|json_script:... }}` needs no nonce

Django emits `<script id="..." type="application/json">` (`django/utils/html.py:106`). A
non-JS `type` makes the element a *data block*: HTML's prepare-the-script-element algorithm
returns before the CSP inline-behavior check, so it is neither executed nor policy-checked,
and it is read via `.textContent`, which CSP never touches. Three such tags exist
(`auth_base.html`, `register.html` ×2); none get a nonce. **This corrects the workspec**,
which lists `json_script` as part of what makes a strict `script-src` hard.

### D5 — Scope: hosted auth pages only

Do **not** build a settings-gated framework-wide default. A nonce is only valid for a
response whose markup was stamped with the same value; blanket middleware cannot know which
templates are nonce-aware. `bouncer_challenge.html`, `bouncer_decoy.html`,
`email_change_confirm.html` and `email_verify_confirm.html` all carry un-nonce'd inline
content and would break. Note `render_ctx.css_nonce` in the challenge page is an
anti-automation class-name randomizer, **not** a CSP nonce — do not conflate them.

### D6 — Override mechanism: three file-only settings, read PER REQUEST

| Key | Read | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED` | `settings.get_static(..., kind="bool")` | `True` | `False` → no header at all |
| `AUTH_CSP_REPORT_ONLY` | `settings.get_static(..., kind="bool")` | `False` | `True` → `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` |
| `AUTH_CSP_DIRECTIVES` | `settings.get_static(..., kind="dict")` | `{}` | per-directive merge over the defaults |

Merge semantics: a present key **replaces** that directive wholesale; an empty value
**drops** the directive; an unknown key is **emitted as-is** (so a deployment can add
`report-uri`). The per-request nonce is always appended to the final `script-src` and
cannot be removed — `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED=False` is the opt-out.

`get_static` (file-only), **not** `settings.get(..., group=group)`: a security header is a
deploy-time decision and a DB/Redis `Setting` row (writable through the generic
`/api/settings` REST plane) must never weaken it. Precedent:
`AUTH_PHONE_VERIFY_DEV_BYPASS_CODE`, `MOJO_TEST_MODE`.

**All three MUST be read inside `default_directives()` / `build_policy()` / `apply()` — never
at module import.** The dominant idiom in this app is import-time `get_static`
(`bouncer/views.py:30,73,227,425`, `bouncer/static.py:26`, `login_event.py:8-10`); following
it here would make every settings test a silent no-op and make the settings undeployable
without a restart. See Challenge O2.

### D7 — Nonce mechanics

Generated in `_auth_context()` as `ctx['csp_nonce'] = secrets.token_hex(16)` (`secrets` is
already imported at `views.py:14`). `_auth_context` is the single funnel for all four pages.
A small helper reads the same `ctx` and stamps the header, so header and markup can never
disagree. `MojoMiddleware` sets `Cache-Control: no-store` on every response
(`mojo/middleware/mojo.py:69`, unconditional and applied after `get_response`), so a nonce'd
page is never cached; `dispatch_error_handler` returns any `HttpResponse` untouched
(`http.py:161-163`).

### Implementation steps

**Step 0 — batch hazard check (mandatory, before any edit).** #943 and #958 land before this
item and both touch these files. Run
`git log --oneline -8 -- mojo/apps/account/templates/account/ mojo/apps/account/static/account/mojo-auth.js`
and re-read `auth_base.html` in full. **All line numbers below are pre-batch and WILL have
drifted — anchor on the named markers, not the numbers.** The only edits to `auth_base.html`
are the two `<script>` **open tags**; do not copy, move, retype, or reformat any line inside
the IIFE body. Then re-run `grep -n "<script" mojo/apps/account/templates/account/*.html` and
nonce every inline block you find — do not trust this plan's inventory of six tags without
re-deriving it. (#958's approved plan adds no new script tags and no new script origins, so
the inventory is expected to hold; verify anyway.)

**Step 1 — new `mojo/apps/account/services/csp.py`.** Module docstring covering scope, the
nonce contract, why `style-src`/`img-src` are permissive, the per-page `frame-ancestors`
rule, and the three settings. No type hints. Public surface:
- `HEADER = "Content-Security-Policy"`, `REPORT_ONLY_HEADER = "Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only"`
- `DIRECTIVE_ORDER` tuple in the D2 order (fixed emission order → byte-stable header)
- `_origin(url)` — `scheme://netloc` via `urllib.parse.urlsplit`, `""` for empty/relative
- `default_directives(api_base="", frame_ancestors="'none'")` — the baseline dict; appends
  `_origin(api_base)` to `style-src` and `connect-src` when non-empty; drops
  `frame-ancestors` when `frame_ancestors` is falsy
- `build_policy(nonce, api_base="", frame_ancestors="'none'")` — baseline → merge
  `AUTH_CSP_DIRECTIVES` → append `'nonce-<nonce>'` to `script-src` → emit `DIRECTIVE_ORDER`
  first then extra keys, skipping empty values, joined with `"; "`
- `apply(response, nonce, api_base="", frame_ancestors="'none'")` — returns `response`
  unchanged when `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED` is false; else sets `HEADER` (or `REPORT_ONLY_HEADER`
  when `AUTH_CSP_REPORT_ONLY`) and returns it

**Step 2 — `mojo/apps/account/rest/bouncer/views.py`.**
- `_auth_context()` gains `'csp_nonce': secrets.token_hex(16),`.
- New private helper — name it **`_render_with_csp`**, NOT `_render_auth_page`
  (`tests/test_auth_config/auth_config.py:285` already defines a module-level helper by that
  name; different module, no real collision, but the name is taken in the reader's head):
  ```
  def _render_with_csp(request, template, ctx, frame_ancestors="'none'"):
      from mojo.apps.account.services import csp
      response = render(request, template, ctx)
      return csp.apply(response, ctx.get('csp_nonce', ''),
                       api_base=ctx.get('api_base', ''),
                       frame_ancestors=frame_ancestors)
  ```
- Route all four render sites through it: `on_passkey_enroll_page`, both branches of
  `_serve_login` (register + login), and `_serve_contact` — the contact site passes
  `frame_ancestors=""`. Leave `_serve_challenge` and `_serve_decoy` alone.

**Step 3 — templates (open tags only).** `auth_base.html`: the external
`<script src="{{ api_base }}/api/account/static/mojo-auth.js">` and the inline `<script>`
both gain `nonce="{{ csp_nonce }}"`. Then `login.html`, `register.html`,
`passkey_enroll.html`, `contact.html` — each inline `<script>` → `<script nonce="{{ csp_nonce }}">`.
Leave every `json_script` tag untouched.

**Step 4 — tests: `tests/test_auth/csp.py`** (see Testing plan).

**Step 5 — docs + CHANGELOG** (see Documentation plan).

### Edge cases

- **Cross-origin `api_base`**: handled by the nonce on the `mojo-auth.js` tag plus the
  `api_origin` term in `style-src`/`connect-src`. Covered by a unit test.
- **Whitelabel assets**: any-origin `logo_url`/`hero_image_url`/`favicon_url` → `img-src * data:`;
  tenant `custom_css_url` (https-validated) and inline `custom_css` →
  `style-src ... 'unsafe-inline' https:`. Nothing breaks.
- **Deployment-overridden templates**: `auth_pages.md` documents that any `account/*.html` can
  be overridden. A deployment shipping its own `auth_base.html` or `{% block page_script %}`
  with un-nonce'd inline scripts will have them blocked. Mitigations, all documented: add
  `nonce="{{ csp_nonce }}"` (the context key is always present), `AUTH_CSP_REPORT_ONLY=True`
  to observe first, or `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED=False`. This is the single real upgrade risk and
  belongs in the CHANGELOG as an explicit "what to check before upgrading".
- **`csp_nonce` missing from context** would render `nonce=""` and block the script.
  Structurally guarded: `_auth_context` is the only context builder for these four templates.
  `_serve_contact` does `ctx.update(kind_ctx)`, and `render_context_for_kind` returns only
  `kind`/`kind_title`/`kind_subtitle`/fields, so it cannot clobber the key.
- **`/auth`, `/register`, `/contact` are bouncer-gated.** A cold client is served
  `bouncer_challenge.html`, which gets **no** CSP header by design. Document that the header
  appears on the real page (post-challenge, or with an `mbp` pass cookie), not on the challenge.
- **`X-Mojo-Test-*` header override**: deliberately not added — it would grow the
  remotely-armable test-header surface for two tests that in-process settings mutation covers.

### Testing plan (`tests/test_auth/csp.py`)

`test_auth` already declares `requires_apps: ["mojo.apps.account"]`. New files are
auto-discovered — no registration needed. Every assert carries a descriptive message. Setup
cleans up before creating. Do **not** run the suite — the batch has one closing run.

Key enabler: **`GET /passkey` is not bouncer-gated** (only `@md.GET` + `@md.public_endpoint`;
no challenge branch, unlike `on_login_page`/`on_contact_page`). It renders `passkey_enroll.html`,
which extends `auth_base.html` — the one hosted auth page whose real response headers
`opts.client` can assert. **Read headers case-insensitively** —
`testit/client.py:143` does `dict(response.headers)`, discarding `requests`'
`CaseInsensitiveDict`, and header-name casing differs between `h11` and `httptools`. Use
`{k.lower(): v for k, v in opts.client.last_response.headers.items()}` (the idiom at
`tests/test_limits/api_throttle.py:65`). See Challenge O3.

**Live-server (no `server_settings`, no restarts) — asserts the shipped defaults only:**
1. `GET /passkey` → 200, header present, containing each of `default-src 'self'`,
   `base-uri 'none'`, `object-src 'none'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `form-action 'self'`,
   `script-src `, `style-src `, `img-src `, `connect-src `.
2. Parse `script-src` out of the header: `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` absent, no bare
   `*` / `http:` / `https:` source, exactly one `'nonce-<32 hex>'`.
3. **The honest reading of "a known-bad inline injection is blocked."** No browser runs in the
   suite, so nothing can be executed and blocked. Assert the two properties that jointly
   *produce* the block: (a) `script-src` has a nonce and no `unsafe-inline`; (b) over the
   response body, every `re.finditer(r'<script([^>]*)>', body)` match either contains
   `nonce="<the header's nonce>"` or `type="application/json"`. Any script text that did not
   come from a nonce-stamped template tag therefore lacks the nonce and cannot run. This also
   becomes the regression guard against a future un-nonce'd block. **State this
   reinterpretation in the test module docstring; do not claim the test proves browser
   enforcement.**
4. Two sequential `GET /passkey` calls → different nonces, each body's script tags carrying
   its own.
5. `mat-login-methods` renders as `type="application/json"` with no nonce — documents the
   deliberate data-block exemption.

**In-process (direct calls, no server):**
6. Render all four templates through `RequestFactory` + `_auth_context` +
   `django.shortcuts.render` (pattern at `tests/test_auth_config/auth_config.py:285-296`) and
   apply the same "nonce'd or `application/json`" invariant using `ctx['csp_nonce']`. This is
   what catches a child template someone forgot.
7. `build_policy('abc', api_base='https://api.example.com')` → `connect-src` and `style-src`
   contain the origin; `script-src` does not.
8. Whitelabel guard: `img-src` permits any origin and `data:`; `style-src` contains
   `'unsafe-inline'`.
9. **Per-page `frame-ancestors`**: `build_policy('abc')` contains `frame-ancestors 'none'`;
   `build_policy('abc', frame_ancestors="")` omits the directive entirely. Plus an in-process
   render assertion that the contact response carries no `frame-ancestors` while the other
   three do.
10-14. Settings behavior — **call `csp.apply(HttpResponse(), 'x')` / `build_policy` directly**;
   these cannot be asserted against the live server (its settings are loaded at startup and
   never see a test-process patch). Override in-process with
   `setattr(django.conf.settings, KEY, value)` in `try/finally` with a `_SENTINEL`
   save/restore (idiom at `tests/test_geofence/test_override_file_only.py:34-45`); no other
   module reads `AUTH_CSP_*`, so the mutation races nothing. Cover: a directive replaced
   (`frame-ancestors 'self'`); one added (`report-uri`) and one dropped (`font-src: ""`); the
   nonce still appended to a deployment-supplied `script-src`; `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED=False` → neither
   header set; `AUTH_CSP_REPORT_ONLY=True` → report-only header set, enforcing header absent.

Regression check on existing suites (no changes expected, but verify):
`tests/test_auth_config/auth_config.py`, `tests/test_auth/bouncer_forms.py`,
`tests/test_register/passkey_prompt.py`, `tests/test_auth/sms_otp_autofill.py`,
`tests/test_auth/oauth_callback_single_fire.py`, `tests/test_public_messages/4_contact_page.py`.
None assert on a literal `<script>` string.

### Documentation plan

1. **New `docs/django_developer/security/csp.md`** — which responses carry the header and which
   deliberately don't; the full default policy with per-directive rationale; **the per-page
   `frame-ancestors` rule and why `/contact` is exempt**; the nonce contract
   (`{{ csp_nonce }}` in any overridden template); why `style-src`/`img-src` are permissive;
   the three settings and their merge rules; the report-only rollout path; and the non-goal —
   consuming applications own their own pages' CSP.
2. **`docs/django_developer/security/README.md`** — bullet in "Related Documentation".
3. **`docs/django_developer/account/auth_pages.md`** — new "Content Security Policy"
   subsection after the Templates block: if you override a template or add inline JS via
   `{% block page_script %}` / `{% block extra_css %}`, stamp `nonce="{{ csp_nonce }}"`.
4. **`docs/django_developer/helpers/settings_reference.md`** — `AUTH_CSP_DIRECTIVES`,
   `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED`, `AUTH_CSP_REPORT_ONLY` under `### AUTH`, alphabetical, each noting
   **file-only** (`settings.get_static`), linking to `../security/csp.md`.
5. **`docs/web_developer/account/auth_pages.md`** — short subsection: the login/register/passkey
   pages now refuse to be embedded in an iframe. No REST endpoint, payload or status change.
6. **`docs/web_developer/account/public_messages.md`** — the "Integrating from an External
   Marketing Site" section keeps recommending the `/contact` iframe; add a sentence stating
   `/contact` deliberately omits `frame-ancestors` for exactly this reason, and that a
   deployment which adds it via `AUTH_CSP_DIRECTIVES` breaks the iframe option.
7. **`CHANGELOG.md`** — lead with the observable change (`frame-ancestors 'none'`: the
   login/register/passkey pages can no longer be iframed; `/contact` is unaffected), the

### Schema impact

None. No models, fields or migrations. `bin/create_testproject` is **not** needed. No new
test-project settings — all three keys default to their shipping values and the tests override
in-process.

### Contract changes

- **New response header on four routes**: the login, register, passkey and contact pages
  (post-challenge where gated). Challenge/decoy pages, email-confirm pages and every JSON API
  response are unchanged.
- **`frame-ancestors 'none'` on login/register/passkey is the one observable behavior change** —
  no `X-Frame-Options` or CSP exists today, so those pages are currently framable by any
  origin. `/contact` deliberately keeps its framability.
- **Template contract**: any template extending `account/auth_base.html`, and any deployment
  override of these templates, must stamp `nonce="{{ csp_nonce }}"` on inline `<script>` tags
  or they will not execute.
- **`_auth_context()` gains `csp_nonce`** — additive; nine existing test modules call it
  directly and are unaffected.
- Three new optional settings.

### Challenge

Red-team returned 6 objections; 1 blocking, all disposed.

- **O1 `frame-ancestors 'none'` breaks a documented consumer integration — AMENDED (was
  blocking).** `docs/web_developer/account/public_messages.md:221` recommends embedding
  `/contact?kind=<kind>` in an iframe as the least-work integration for an external marketing
  site. Verified in the doc. The plan's "no framework flow iframes them" check was scoped to
  *framework* flows and structurally could not catch a consumer path documented in the
  web_developer track. A global CSP toggle would force such a deployment to disable CSP on the
  token-holding pages too. Fix: `frame-ancestors` is per-page (D3) — `'none'` on
  login/register/passkey, omitted on `/contact` — plus a doc note and a test asserting both
  shapes.
- **O2 settings read at import would make every settings test a silent no-op — AMENDED.** The
  app's dominant idiom is module-level `get_static`; the plan didn't forbid it. D6 now requires
  per-request reads, and the settings tests call `csp.apply()`/`build_policy()` directly rather
  than asserting against a live server whose settings were fixed at startup.
- **O3 header lookup must be case-normalized — AMENDED.** `testit/client.py:143` flattens
  `requests`' `CaseInsensitiveDict` into a plain dict; `h11` and `httptools` differ on casing.
  Two existing test modules already defend against this. Testing plan now specifies the
  lowercase-normalized lookup.
- **O4 the `connect-src` audit missed `contact.html`'s own `fetch` — AMENDED (record only).**
  `contact.html` builds `submitUrl` from the same `api_base` and fetches it, so
  `connect-src 'self' <api_origin>` already covers it — the directive was right, the
  verification record was incomplete. Now named in D2.
- **O5 line numbers will drift; #958's plan is now known — AMENDED.** Step 0 already required
  re-deriving the inventory at build time. Confirmed against #958's approved plan: it adds no
  new inline script tags and no new script origins, so the six-tag inventory is expected to
  hold — the builder verifies anyway.
- **O6 nine test modules call `_auth_context`, not five; `_render_auth_page` name is taken —
  AMENDED (record only).** All nine build ctx via `_auth_context`, so the additive `csp_nonce`
  renders populated in every one; zero impact. The new view helper is named `_render_with_csp`.

**Value assessment (the scope pass of #943 called this item "closeable as low value" — that
was wrong).** The headline win is not `script-src`, it is `frame-ancestors`: the framework
ships **zero** anti-framing today (no `X-Frame-Options`, no `XFrameOptionsMiddleware` in the
reference config, no CSP), so the highest-value pages it serves — the ones holding access and
refresh tokens in `localStorage` — are framable by any origin right now. That is a missing
standard control, not a hypothetical, and it costs one directive. The cost is also lower than
the workspec assumed: via nonces this is six one-line template edits, a ~60-line service, four
call sites and a settings triple — not the inline-JS relocation the workspec feared. Ship it.

### Baseline

Per `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`, the batch baseline was captured once before any edit:
**3016 tests, 2959 passed, 1 failed, 56 skipped** (full-suite totals: 385 skipped incl. opt-in
modules). The single failure is `test_geofence > config: DELETE geo/rules removes the DB
override`, which passes 12/12 in an isolated re-run — a known cross-module shared-state flake
(same family as commit `6048f654`), unrelated to this item. No file in this plan touches
geofence.
